title: Decision readiness, one row per requirement of the 2026-11-19 brief
policy: status is what the repository and today's official reads support, not what a plan intends. 'met' means a reader can check the artifact and the number today; a row that is blocked says which number would clear it, and the desk publishes 0 rather than an estimate where a source is missing.

rows.verbatim: Add a price-snapshot store that records opening and closing numbers for every market we originate
rows.gate: No official or licensed price feed is wired in. nfl.com publishes schedules, scores and designations, never a spread, total or moneyline, so the market columns of every store in the repository stay empty by policy.
rows.clearing_number: 2 timestamps per market per game x 3 markets x 15 Week 11 games = 90 filled slots for one week, each with a licensed source key; 0 filled today.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: 3 stores exist: nfl-markets data/price_snapshots.csv (12573 rows, opening filled on 2587, closing on 12246 - third-party archive, self-declared in FLAG-M1), nfl-book data/price_snapshots.json (39 rows of OUR OWN originated numbers with the market columns null), nfl-availability-desk and nfl-live-board stores at 0 rows by choice.

rows.verbatim: Add a verified results feed so backtests and ROI can be computed at all
rows.gate: nothing blocks played games; the gate is freshness - a feed that lags the official page silently shrinks every sample.
rows.clearing_number: 32 standings rows x games played / 2 = 150 games for the 2026 regular season so far; a feed must equal that number every day.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: THIS SESSION closed a real gap: the two feeds in the repo disagreed (nfl-markets 2026 = 137 games, Week 10 = 1 game; nfl-live-board corpus = 149). Re-reading the official Week 10 page gives 14 finals; 149 - 150 = 1 game (LAC 23 at BAL 20) was missing everywhere, and the standings identity sum(W+L+T)/2 = 150 now matches the extended corpus exactly.

rows.verbatim: Originate the side first, then the total, then the moneyline
rows.gate: no gate - this is an ordering rule and the live register follows it.
rows.clearing_number: 3 ordered stage columns per fixture in every record; 13 of 13 Week 11 fixtures carry stage 1 and 2, and stage 3 is derived from stage 1 rather than fitted.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: nfl-live-board/data/origination_week11.json records stage_1 side, stage_2 total, stage_3 moneyline with the explicit note that the moneyline is derived from the margin distribution and never fitted separately.

rows.verbatim: Publish the model's fair line, the market line, and the difference as separate columns
rows.gate: the market column cannot be filled without a licensed price source; the difference column is therefore blank too. Filling it with an assumed -110 is the failure mode the earlier namespaces were criticised for.
rows.clearing_number: 3 columns x 3 markets x 15 games = 135 cells per week, of which the fair-line 45 are publishable today; 0 of the 90 market/difference cells are fillable without a price feed.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: the desk publishes fair line, market line (null + reason) and residual (null) as three separate columns for all 13 Week 11 fixtures.

rows.verbatim: Separate 'signal' from 'staking' in the leaderboard so a lucky staking run cannot mask a bad signal
rows.status: met as a rule, division empty
rows.gate: a staking division cannot open before either (a) a graded pre-kickoff sample or (b) a licensed price feed exists. Both are absent.
rows.clearing_number: signal division opens at 300 graded pre-kickoff rows; staking division opens only after the signal division clears its lower bound AND 90 price slots per week are being captured.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: every workspace reports 0 rewards; the only graded-able object today is a 13-row shadow record with 0 graded rows, so the two divisions are published empty rather than merged.

rows.verbatim: Track the depth of the replacement, not just the fact of a replacement
rows.gate: depth of a replacement needs either a verified per-club depth register or an official snap-count source. Club depth pages are verified for 31 of 32 clubs (HOU publishes an image); no official snap-count source has been located.
rows.clearing_number: 32 of 32 clubs with a dated, hashed depth capture (or an official snap-count table) would clear it; today it is 31 of 32 with 0 snap counts.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: nfl-depth-sweep holds per-club captures and a roster/IR sweep (25 November reserve entries, 5 stale-depth flags); the desk's own K07 correlation is blank with n=0 because the input does not exist yet.

rows.verbatim: Compute correlations only from officially sourced numbers and publish n with each value
rows.gate: nothing blocks the schedule-and-score correlations; the availability and price correlations are blocked by missing dated sources and are published blank with n=0 rather than estimated.
rows.clearing_number: every published value carries n; 4 computed values (n=150, 150, 134, 268) and 3 explicit blanks with reasons today.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: the desk computed K01 margin~total r=-0.1405 (n=150), K02 away~home r=0.0486 (n=150), K03 rest~margin r=0.3256 (n=134), K04 persistence r=0.1359 (n=268) from the 2026 corpus only, each with a Fisher-z interval and a 20,000-step permutation test at seed 20261119.

rows.verbatim: Define a demotion gate that sends a live strategy back to paper
rows.status: defined, nothing to apply it to
rows.gate: the gate needs a live strategy; none exists, because nothing has been promoted.
rows.clearing_number: 0 strategies live today (so 0 demotions possible); the gate fires at the first game-cluster lower bound <= 0 over a trailing 4-week window, or on one missed report cycle of a required feed.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: the rule text and its today-status are published as a row, not as a claim: 'strategies_live: 0, demotions_today: 0, nothing to demote'.

rows.verbatim: Pre-register every strategy; forbid backtest numbers from ever appearing on the leaderboard
rows.gate: the ban is a publication rule, and it is enforced by the leaderboard generator refusing a row whose provenance is 'backtest'.
rows.clearing_number: 1 registration commit hash per strategy, and 0 backtest rows on any leaderboard page; both hold today.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: nfl-readiness/prereg/SHADOW_BASELINE_v1.md is a frozen rule whose commit is the registration (sha256 published by the desk); nfl-markets publishes a large 2011-2026 backtest but labels it as a backtest in its own decisions file and its leaderboard carries no reward row, which is the compliant pattern.

rows.verbatim: Build the availability graph as a first-class dataset (who was expected to start, who actually did)
rows.gate: 'expected to start' needs the dated depth register; 'actually did' needs the official inactive list and the Game Book participation table, which the repository does not hold. Only the first half can be built from what is licensed today.
rows.clearing_number: 2 edges per club per position per week (expected -> actual) with both endpoints sourced; today 0 edges have an 'actual' endpoint because no inactive list is stored anywhere.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: the desk publishes the 'expected' side from two dated reads and shows the missing side as a named hole, not as a blank row.

rows.verbatim: Do not model depth from jersey order; model it from playing time
rows.gate: playing time means snap counts; there is no official snap-count dataset in the repository and none located on an official NFL page. The Packers' jersey-prefix parsing failure is a separate defect, fixed by storing the raw string alongside the stripped value.
rows.clearing_number: 1 official playing-time source with a dated capture for 32 clubs; today 0.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: the desk refuses to substitute jersey order: K07 (replacement depth) is published as n=0 with the reason.

rows.gate: a surprise needs two dated reads of the same report; the repository had exactly one before 2026-11-18, which is why every earlier surprise column was blank.
rows.clearing_number: 2 dated reads minimum per report cycle, 3 recommended (Wed/Thu/Fri); the desk now holds 2 for Week 11 and turns them into 1 measured surprise.

rows.verbatim: Add a fixture-context feature set built only from published schedule facts
rows.gate: no gate; the rule is exclusionary - roof, weather and travel are excluded until an official/licensed source exists, and the exclusion is stated on the page.
rows.clearing_number: N features x 150 games, each traceable to a date, a venue or a network slot on an official page; rest-day features today cover 134 of 150 games (a club's first appearance has no prior date).
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: the desk re-measured the strongest schedule-only relationship on the extended corpus: rest differential vs home margin r=0.3256 (n=134, permutation p=0.0003).

rows.verbatim: Store every model output as a probability plus its inputs, not just a pick
rows.gate: no gate - this is a storage shape, and the desk's cohort record writes inputs (W/L/T/PF/PA per club), constants (SIGMA, HFA), the margin, both probabilities and both control picks per row.
rows.clearing_number: 100% of recorded rows carrying an 'inputs' object; 13 of 13 Week 11 rows do.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: the desk also re-derived the 5 stored cohort-1 rows from the frozen rule and today's official standings: 5 of 5 matched field for field, which proves the record is reproducible rather than hand-written.

rows.verbatim: Compute and publish the "removal of luck" panel on the site dashboard
rows.status: met as controls, not as a claim
rows.gate: luck can only be removed against a benchmark; the benchmark needs either a graded sample (0 games today) or a price (absent). The honest panel is therefore the control baselines plus the sample-size refusal.
rows.clearing_number: 300 graded pre-kickoff rows before any skill number is published; 0 graded today, and the panel says so.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: controls measured from the 150-game official 2026 corpus: always-home 0.4733, coin-flip 0.5, Week 10 home 0.2857 (4 of 14) - the home baseline is BELOW a coin flip this season, so any 'home edge' prior is wrong, and a model that merely picks home is a negative-skill model.

rows.verbatim: Add a two-sided "what would change our mind" field to every strategy entry
rows.gate: no gate; every strategy row needs both a FOR and an AGAINST clause or it is not listed.
rows.clearing_number: 2 clauses per strategy row; the single registered strategy (singles shadow v1) carries both in its rule text, quoted by the desk.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: nfl-readiness/prereg/SHADOW_BASELINE_v1.md states evidence for (BSS lower bound > 0 after 300 graded games and beating the favourites control) and against (upper bound < 0, or a worse Brier than the coin flip over 4 consecutive weeks).

rows.gate: our side of the residual is published; the market side needs the price feed decision (R-20). 'On a schedule' also needs the cadence to be tied to report and line publication times, not to whenever a capture happens to run.
rows.clearing_number: 3 residuals per fixture per week from the first graded week (45 for Week 11); 0 computable today.

rows.as_of_2026_11_19: identity verified today: 32 standings rows imply 150 games; the extended 2026 corpus holds 150; total points from standings (6,923) equals total points in the corpus exactly.

rows.verbatim: Decide the price-data policy before any backtest is published

Backtests under (c) already exist in the repo with the label disclosed.
rows.clearing_number: 1 written policy + 1 source key per price row; 0 policies recorded in COORDINATION.md as an owner decision.
rows.as_of_2026_11_19: measured today, the consequence of the gap: nfl-markets fills 12,246 of 12,573 closing cells and 2,587 opening cells with a third-party archive; two namespaces (nfl-availability-desk, nfl-live-board) hold 0 price rows by policy; nfl-book holds 39 rows that are OUR numbers, not the market's.
